title.narrative: Access to quality, equitable, and Safe Learning Environments for Crisis-Affected Children and Communities in Machekel, Enemay , Sedae and Goncha Siso Enebse districts of East Gojam Zone

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe ongoing conflict in the Amhara Region has severely impacted education, leaving over 4.1 million children—59.5% of the targeted enrollment—out of school. Only 2.7 million (39.45%) students remain enrolled across 7,059 schools, as Humanitarian Review in April 2025 indicated the situation is particularly dire in East Gojam three districts, Machakel, Enemay Sedae and Goncha Siso EnebseltbrgtDEC recent Preliminary assessment indicates that, in Machakel , 56 schools remain closed (out of 60 school), 19 partially damaged. ltbrgtn Enemay , 58 schools remain closed (out of 76 school), 46 partially damaged. In Sedae district, has only 4 out of 33 schools functioning. In the three districts, only 25 schools out of 169 schools are functioning. As a result in districts, over 38,186 children have been denied their right to education, learning environments have become unsafe, gender-based violence has escalated, and education quality has deteriorated. A recent preliminary assessment by DEC highlights a fractured education system requiring urgent intervention.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, this project mainstreams protection actions with education services, creating a holistic and safe learning environment. It aims to enhance access to education, improve education quality, and ensure equity in learning through safe and protective spaces for over 24,725(60 % girls) in targeted districts Machakel, Enemay and Sedae.ltbrgtTo achieve these outcomes, the project will facilitate non formal learning - Accelerated Learning Programs for 2800 out-of-school children and including home-based learning facilitation . It will distribute scholastic materials to 18,253 students. Additionally, 45 classrooms and 8 latrines with WASH facilities will be renovated to create a safe and protective learning environment.ltbrgtThe project will also maintain 700 chairs and tables, conduct back-to-school campaigns across 17 schools, and train over 700 teachers, school leaders, and education experts in pedagogical methods, gender-sensitive teaching, inclusive education, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). Over 1,800 reference and supplementary materials will be provided to targeted schools, while 17 schools will receive teaching materials.ltbrgtFurthermore, 300 children will be supported through referral linkages, and over 1,000 children will attend make-up classes to compensate for lost learning. Gender clubs will be strengthened in 17 schools, and 500 schoolgirls will receive menstrual hygiene kits. The project will also provide assistive devices for 60 children with disabilities and engage 4,500 children in socio-emotional learning activities.ltbrgtTo support mental health and psychosocial well-being, over 30,000 children will benefit from sport-based interventions. More than 1,000 parents will receive training on parenting, lifesaving measures, early warning mechanisms, disability inclusion, and gender-based violence (GBV) awareness. School staff, communities, and parents will be trained in Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and safeguarding, and community-based complaint-handling mechanisms will be strengthened to ensure safety and accountability.ltbrgtThis project will be implemented by national CSOs: DEC lead, and ASDEPO as sub grantee. Both organizations prioritize community empowerment and sustainable service delivery by reinforcing existing local structures and promoting local ownership and support communities in shaping development agendas, ensuring accountability to affected persons.ltbrgtRecognizing potential risks such as security concerns, mobility restrictions, and resource shortages, mitigation measures will include coordinated efforts, stakeholder engagement, and adaptive planning. Participatory monitoring involving local stakeholders will ensure continuous assessment, compliance with agency requirements, and the effectiveness of interventions.ltbrgtlt/pgt
